notes: Both coders found the same single CETL template and agreed on document stance (delegates). Main disagreements: (1) phase and modality for statements that are really instructor-discretion or classification (e.g. the 'what uses constitute academic dishonesty' clause, the P36 'will violate' sentence, the placeholder penalty line), resolved by rereading the sentence for what it actually does; (2) type for the bracketed 'You may [or may not]' template lines (A: P92 and UNCOVERED, B: P04), resolved to P04 because the instructor, not the university, sets the rule, with A's UNCOVERED note preserved in fit_note; (3) 'ok to ask' (A: P66, B: P10), resolved to P10; (4) 'encourage transparency' (A: P24, B: P28), resolved to P24 since nothing says disclosure is made safe; (5) unit_stance for P24/P29/P31 units (A set require, B permit/neutral), resolved by whether the unit takes a position on AI use itself; (6) granularity: B split bracketed example lists into extra permission units (P15, P91, P31), dropped as over-splitting; A split the bans-are-hard sentence's three premises and kept them. Only-A units kept: embedded-AI unclear sentence, two ban-difficulty premises, the generative AI definition, and the 'language only suggested' clause; A's academic-integrity procedure sentence dropped as not about AI. Only-B units: two example splits and a verbatim repeat, all dropped.
